- The walls absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night, keeping interiors cool in the daytime.
- Neither method requires electricity or machinery.
items.stem: The student wants to make a generalization about traditional buildings in hot climates. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: In Yazd, Iran, windcatchers built on traditional houses capture breezes and direct them down into the rooms below.
Pueblo dwellings have thick adobe walls that absorb heat during the day and release it slowly at night.

Traditional buildings in hot climates, from the windcatcher houses of Yazd, Iran, to the adobe Pueblo dwellings of the southwestern United States, have used designs that cool their interiors without electricity or machinery.
Unlike windcatchers, which capture breezes, the adobe walls of Pueblo dwellings absorb heat during the day.

explanation.en: A generalization makes a broad statement that covers many cases. Only the sentence about 'traditional buildings in hot climates' cooling 'without electricity or machinery', supported by both examples, does this. The Yazd and Pueblo sentences each describe a single case, and the 'Unlike windcatchers' sentence contrasts the two methods instead of stating what they share.
explanation.th: การสรุปกว้าง (generalization) ต้องกล่าวข้อความที่ครอบคลุมหลายกรณี มีเพียงประโยคที่บอกว่า 'อาคารดั้งเดิมในเขตร้อน' ใช้การออกแบบที่ทำให้ภายในเย็นได้ 'โดยไม่ใช้ไฟฟ้าหรือเครื่องจักร' และยกทั้งสองตัวอย่างมาประกอบ ประโยคเรื่องเมือง Yazd และเรื่อง Pueblo พูดถึงเพียงกรณีเดียว ส่วนประโยค Unlike windcatchers เป็นการเปรียบเทียบความต่าง ไม่ใช่สิ่งที่มีร่วมกัน

topic.th: จิตวิทยา

items.passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
- In a 2000 study, shoppers at a grocery store saw a display of either 24 or 6 varieties of jam.
- 30% of shoppers who saw 6 jams bought one; only 3% of those who saw 24 jams did.
- The researchers concluded that too many options can discourage people from choosing at all.
- In 2010, a team of psychologists analyzed the results of 50 experiments on this "choice overload" effect.
- On average, the number of options had virtually no effect on whether people made a choice.
items.stem: The student wants to present the 2010 analysis as a challenge to the conclusion of the 2000 study. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?
choices: A 2000 study found that 30% of shoppers who saw 6 jams bought one, while only 3% of those who saw 24 jams did.

Although a 2000 study concluded that too many options can discourage people from choosing, a 2010 analysis of 50 experiments found that, on average, the number of options had virtually no effect on whether people chose.
In 2010, a team of psychologists analyzed the results of 50 experiments on the "choice overload" effect.
Both a 2000 study and a 2010 analysis examined how the number of available options affects people's decisions.

explanation.en: To present the analysis as a challenge, the sentence must state the 2000 conclusion and set the 2010 finding against it. Only the 'Although…' sentence does both. The jam percentages give only the 2000 results; the 2010 sentence omits what the analysis found; the 'Both…' sentence stresses what the studies share rather than how they conflict.
explanation.th: การเสนอผลปี 2010 ให้เป็นการท้าทายต้องระบุข้อสรุปของปี 2000 และนำผลปี 2010 มาแย้ง ประโยค Although… ทำได้ครบ ส่วนประโยคร้อยละของแยมให้เพียงผลปี 2000 ประโยคเรื่องการวิเคราะห์ปี 2010 ไม่ได้บอกผลที่พบ และประโยค Both… เน้นสิ่งที่เหมือนกันแทนที่จะเป็นข้อขัดแย้ง

topic.th: เศรษฐศาสตร์

items.passage: Standard economic models predict that raising a minimum wage will reduce employment among low-wage workers. In a 1994 study, economists David Card and Alan Krueger compared fast-food restaurants in New Jersey, which had just raised its minimum wage, with restaurants in neighboring Pennsylvania, which had not, and found no decline in employment in New Jersey. ______ the study did not settle the debate: later analyses of restaurants in the same areas using payroll records rather than telephone surveys reached conflicting conclusions.
items.stem: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
choices: Accordingly,
In particular,
Even so,
Likewise,

explanation.en: The Card–Krueger finding might seem to resolve the question, but the next sentence says it did not settle the debate. 'Even so' introduces a point that holds despite what was just said. 'Accordingly' would mean the finding caused the debate to remain open, 'In particular' introduces a specific detail of the previous point, and 'Likewise' signals similarity.
explanation.th: ผลการศึกษาของ Card และ Krueger ดูเหมือนจะยุติข้อถกเถียงได้ แต่ประโยคถัดไปบอกว่า 'ไม่ได้ยุติ' จึงใช้ Even so (ถึงกระนั้น) ซึ่งนำข้อความที่ยังเป็นจริงแม้จะมีข้อมูลก่อนหน้า Accordingly ทำให้ดูเหมือนผลการศึกษาเป็นเหตุให้ข้อถกเถียงยังไม่จบ In particular ใช้ขยายรายละเอียดเฉพาะ และ Likewise แสดงความคล้ายกัน
